No game binaries, firmware or other Sony material are included—port authors supply legally obtained PS2 ELFs.
evidenceScope: Upstream README describes an experimental static recompiler with modules ps2xAnalyzer, ps2xRecomp, ps2xRuntime and ps2xIOP, a recommended Ghidra export workflow for retail or stripped ELFs, and documented limits (VU/GS performance and partial hardware emulation). The repository presents it as a tool for making native PC ports. No REA involvement is claimed.
licenseNote: GPL-3.0 covers this project. Sony firmware, encryption keys and game data are not included; users must supply their own legally obtained PS2 ELF or game files. The README notes inspiration from N64Recomp and use of ELFIO, toml11, fmt and PCSX2 as a runtime reference; those components keep their own terms.
status: Active (default branch main); README labels the project experimental
limitation: The README describes VU and GS performance as very bad, and hardware emulation as partial with many paths stubbed. Build notes say it is tested mainly with MSVC and that some vector paths need SSE4/AVX. Playability of any given game port built on this toolkit is upstream’s claim. We have not independently tested it.

summary: A CPython bytecode decompiler from the University of Texas at Dallas Systems Security Lab, targeting released Python versions from 3.6 onward: it turns .pyc bytecode back into source, with a hosted web service and a local CLI. Design and evaluation are described in the authors’ IEEE S&P 2025 paper; those results are not treated here as independently re-run.
evidenceScope: Upstream README describes local uv install and CLI use, support for Python 3.6+ (pyenv for 3.6/3.7), an optional Redis translation-model cache, and a warning that the public codebase is optimized for readability and may differ in control-flow accuracy from the web service. licenseNote: GPL-3.0 covers this project. The tool decompiles user-supplied bytecode; it does not ship those inputs. Third-party Python program IP stays with its owners. Translation models and any bundled or downloaded model weights may carry separate terms not restated here.
status: Active (default branch main); latest release v0.1.0
limitation: A local run needs uv (and pyenv for EOL 3.6/3.7). Decompilation uses a translation model; first uncached runs perform model inference, and Redis caching is optional. The README warns that the published tree may regress in control-flow accuracy versus the hosted service. Paper metrics and web-service quality are upstream’s. We have not independently tested it.

evidenceScope: Upstream README describes a Rust port of Ghidra’s decompiler that has since diverged, with CLI, browser and Ghidra extension usage, and NOTICE-style origin from Ghidra. licenseNote: Apache-2.0 covers this project. Ghidra and other third-party components keep their own terms. User-supplied binaries are not shipped.
status: Active (default branch main); latest release v1.997; README calls it an experiment in autonomous refinement
limitation: The README says not all native Ghidra features are supported in the GUI extension. DecBench ranking, “19MB in under 3 minutes” and similar figures are upstream’s and were not independently re-run. The documented REA 3.1.0 headless swap and a Made with REA listing are not treated as evidence that REA was used to develop Kuna. We have not independently tested it.

licenseNote: BSD-2-Clause covers this project. The tool scans user-supplied or local running processes and dumps material for analysis; it does not ship malware samples. Third-party Windows or malware IP stays with its owners.
status: Active (default branch master); latest release v0.4.1.1; also packaged via Chocolatey
limitation: Capability claims are upstream’s. We have not independently tested it.
